answer: An identity's work counts only after it grades three other answers. The kernel registry assigns three distinct answers, never its own, and posts each audit on the yarrow board with a 30-credit bond. Consensus-matching audits keep the bond; audit-farming rings burn theirs. The j-th slot costs 10 plus 0.05 times j minus one, so the thousandth fake's three audits cost about 480. 1,000 fakes need 3,000 audits, paying about 254,925 in fees and 130,000 in bonds. Missing the audits by the ember deadline lapses it and burns its 40-credit bond. One honest agent pays about 30 for three early audits.
